rows_detail.query: what happens if I mix two embedding models in one tenant
rows_detail.answer: Mixing two embedding models in one tenant results in silently wrong retrieval. pgvector will compute cosine similarity between vectors of the same dimension without complaint, but the ranking is garbage that looks exactly like a ranking. The failure is silent because no error or warning is raised. This is described as fatal, not merely suboptimal, because cosines from different models are not on one scale, so neither ranking nor threshold survives the mix.

rows_detail.query: why did writing a file with python change every line ending
rows_detail.answer: Writing a file with Python `Path.write_text()` in default text mode on Windows translates `\n` to `\r\n`, converting the file from LF to CRLF line endings (chunk_id: eda6c34066b95c6fa7aaab16e2f773cf9abd7aecc5a6d38c408031b9e4aa71b7). This happens because Python's default text mode converts newlines on write, but `read_text` universalises newlines on read, so a hash comparison cannot detect the change (chunk_id: c5c2a03b5b79f244f3efe8069a5992d87f4c6e6d774fb0a8ffaa23daa7f66083). The working tree is meant to be LF as set by `.gitattributes`, but the write introduces CRLF, causing `git status` to show the file modified with no content difference (chunk_id: eda6c34066b95c6fa7aaab16e2f773cf9abd7aecc5a6d38c408031b9e4aa71b7; chunk_id: 04fa29f55043a3f08b1186d2911e7960a056264d460a13b045961f1b0ce340c0).

rows_detail.query: what happens to a project's memory when I rename its directory
rows_detail.answer: Renaming a project directory causes a new, empty memory store to appear under the new slug, while the old store with all memos becomes invisible with no error or warning. To preserve history, you must move the old memory store to the new slug directory at rename time.

rows_detail.query: what is wrong with a guard I wrote that always passes
rows_detail.answer: A guard that always passes produces a "false green" — it looks like a control but never actually tests anything. The sharper version of this lesson is that such a guard has a twin: a guard that cannot PASS, which also looks like rigour but never tests. Both are dangerous because they provide a false sense of protection while discarding good work in the case of a false red.

rows_detail.query: can two pytest sessions run at the same time here
rows_detail.answer: No, two pytest sessions cannot run at the same time against the same test database. They collide because `tests/conftest.py` calls `apply_migrations` from a session fixture, and `recall.schema`'s guard refuses the second one with a `ConcurrentMigrator` error. The loser does not fail one test; every test errors at setup, so the run reports e.g. `3 skipped, 62 errors` with no failures at all. This was reproduced deliberately on 2026-08-05 with three concurrent runs of `tests/test_bench_systems.py`: one passed, two errored wholesale. The guidance is to run pytest sessions sequentially, never overlapping, and treat `errors` and `failed` as different evidence: only `failed` means a test caught something.

rows_detail.query: why does the test suite have no default database DSN
rows_detail.answer: The test suite has no default database DSN because tests/conftest.py no longer defaults to localhost:5432; when TEST_DSN is unset it points at port 1, so an unconfigured run skips loudly instead of silently sharing a database. This prevents false-red failures caused by accidentally sharing a database.

rows_detail.query: can two pytest sessions run at the same time here
rows_detail.answer: No, two pytest sessions cannot run at the same time against the same test database. They collide because tests/conftest.py calls apply_migrations from a session fixture, and recall.schema's guard refuses the second one with a ConcurrentMigrator error. The loser does not fail one test; every test errors at setup, so the run reports e.g. '3 skipped, 62 errors' with no failures at all. This was reproduced deliberately on 2026-08-05 with three concurrent runs of tests/test_bench_systems.py: one passed, two errored wholesale. Additionally, two suites on one session database invalidate each other silently, and the symptom 'ConcurrentMigrator in fixture setup' is caused by two pytest processes contending for the schema-migration advisory lock.

rows_detail.query: what happens if I mix two embedding models in one tenant
rows_detail.answer: Mixing two embedding models in one tenant leads to silently wrong retrieval. If the models have different dimensions, pgvector rejects the dimension mismatch and fails fast. If they have the same dimension (e.g., voyage-4 and voyage-code-3 both 1024), the SQL query succeeds but the cosine comparison is between embeddings from different models, producing garbage rankings that appear valid.

rows_detail.query: will re-indexing repair a chunker bug
rows_detail.answer: No, re-indexing will not repair a chunker bug. The evidence states: 'Fixing a chunker-selection bug therefore does **not** repair an affected corpus by re-running `recall index`, the run reports "N unchanged" and leaves every wrongly-split chunk exactly where it was.' To actually rebuild, one must change a different term (embedder or context policy) or delete and re-read the affected sources.

rows_detail.query: what happens to a project's memory when I rename its directory
rows_detail.answer: Renaming the project directory causes its memory store to fork: the store is keyed on the project path, so a fresh, empty store appears under the new slug while the old store keeps all existing memos but becomes invisible—no error or warning, and each session loads the new empty store. To preserve the memory, move `~/.claude/projects/<old-slug>/memory/` into the new slug at rename time.

rows_detail.query: is it enough for a guard to refuse known-bad values
rows_detail.answer: No, refusing known-BAD values is not enough. The evidence states: 'Refusing known-BAD values is a negative check. It closes only the failure modes you thought of, and everything the producer never emits — or that predates the field — walks straight through.' Instead, a guard must require the known-good value: 'The closed form is require the known-good value. It rejects nothing the producer emits and everything it does not.'

rows_detail.query: why did writing a file with python change every line ending
rows_detail.answer: Python's `Path.write_text()` in default text mode translates `\n` to `\r\n` on Windows, converting LF endings to CRLF throughout the file. This makes the entire file appear modified in Git even when the content is otherwise identical.

rows_detail.query: what must happen to a scheduled deadman check when a gate closes early
rows_detail.answer: The scheduled task must be cancelled when the gate closes early because an orphaned deadman is worse than a missing one: it arrives with confident, self-contained instructions and no knowledge that the lane died, so the default behaviour is to re-run a closed experiment and post numbers that invite a reopen.

rows_detail.query: does a clean git status mean I am on the tip of the branch
rows_detail.answer: No. A clean git status does not mean you are on the tip of the branch. A clean working tree only means the working tree matches the current commit; it says nothing about which commit you are on or whether that commit is the latest on the branch. The evidence explicitly notes that a clean status says nothing about which commit you are on, and that a status measured earlier can become stale, e.g. showing 0 behind/0 ahead while the branch is actually 4 commits behind by commit time.
